g.text: Order-then-execute on v6 shards with record and replay (amendment of 2026-10-13)
Inclusion and structural validation: as in the first version
or validation waits for execution or for replay
(P1:1708-1714 makes block validity a syntactic predicate).
Execution: one executor runs block b and records it
[each envelope e of b, in block order]
The run is one valid run among many:
a random candidate pick, and, with or without
the scheduler, any order that the rules allow
Replay: every other node follows the record
[replay fails, or ends at another root]
A root mismatch, an invalid record, or an envelope that fails
the filter at the proposer's own attested root is signed slashing
evidence. Any node proves it by replaying the records.
It never changes block validity after the fact.
Casper core: validity, DAG, fork choice, finality
the one executor of a block, which records the run
replay of the record on every other node
the paper "Cost-Accounted Rho Calculus" (L. G. Meredith, May 2026). P1:a-b cites its lines a to b.
the token supply and the demand of signature s
the decision records of the funding check before execution, and of same-block offers on one purse
the newest finalized block whose canonical record the proposer has replayed, and the root after it. E' is a later one.
one finalized block, and one envelope (a signed user deploy) of it
the canonical order of finalized blocks, and the block before b in it
the record of one run of b: pre-root, verdicts, processed deploys, system work, post-root
the post-root of the canonical record of b
the first record of b that a finalized block cites in Ord, starts at executed(prev(b)) and replays to its stated root
one RSpace communication event: a send that matches a receive
latest-message-driven greedy heaviest-observed subtree fork choice
the last finalized block, and the directed acyclic graph of blocks
protocol version 6, with cost accounting and offered envelopes
